chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Durust, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of this son of mine?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Improve his name, and his discipline, and place him in a good position.'
ai.seo_question: What are the primary rights of parents over their children according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS), the Prophet Muhammad (PBUAH) outlines the foundational duties of parenthood, emphasizing that a child's upbringing begins with the spiritual and social act of naming, followed by moral education (adab), and finally securing their social standing. This triad reflects the Shia emphasis on holistic development, where intellectual and moral discipline are as critical as physical care. The hadith underscores the parent's role as the primary architect of the child's identity and character within the community.
